findings.title: Batched single-zone simulation ignores the Euler sub-step; solver plans off a diverged model in the stiff regime
findings.claim: For any single-zone configuration where ThermalModel._stability_substeps returns n_sub >= 2 (inside the config-flow ranges: slab_thermal_mass <= 0.83 kWh/K with slab_heat_transfer 5.0, or slab_thermal_mass 0.1 with the default 0.8), simulate_trajectory_batch diverges from simulate_trajectory by >= 5.3 degC within 48 steps while the two-zone twin stays bitwise identical, and HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize with the batched jacobian returns status 'optimal' with objective 108.50 / cost 103.81 SEK where the scalar-jac solve of the same inputs gives 54.62 / 30.08 SEK.
findings.mechanism: thermal_model.py:2401-2402 sets dt = dt_hours / n_sub for the sub-step loop, but the single-zone branch of simulate_trajectory_batch integrates with dt_hours per sub-step (:2636-2637) and re-seeds T_room from the initial state on every sub-step of step 0 (:2606). The two-zone branch uses dt. tests/features.py::_grad_parity's only sub-step cell is two-zone, so the single-zone twin is untested there.

evidence.unit: objective units (SEK-equivalent): solve_objective_gap_batch_minus_scalar; parity_diff_slab0.5_k5.0 = 1.27e20 degC, parity_min_diff_single_stiff = 5.283 degC
evidence.machine: Apple M1 8 GB (Darwin 25.6), python 3.13.1, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.18.1, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: ten other auditors on the box, load1 22-72 during the runs; every value is a count/ratio/residual/parity, contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: objective gap +-1 (solver path); parity diffs exact (bitwise 0 is the contract)

perturbation.observed_value: parity diff 0.0 degC; objective gap -0.0000; schedule L1 0.0024 kWh

null_control.value: 0.0 degC on the 3 n_sub=1 cells and on all 49 golden configs; grad_batch_vs_scipy_maxabs_default = 0.0

findings.proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py single-zone branch of simulate_trajectory_batch: integrate with dt (dt_hours/n_sub) and hoist the T_room seed out of the sub-step loop; add a single-zone stiff cell to tests/features.py _grad_parity. No golden drift expected (every fixture has n_sub == 1).

findings.title: With a mixing valve, compute_cop falls as outdoor temperature rises above ~10-17 degC at every flow above the reference
findings.claim: For every throttling-valve install (from_config sets cop_flow_carnot=True), ThermalModel.compute_cop(T_out, flow_temp=F) for F in 45..70 degC peaks at 17..10 degC outdoor and at 20 degC outdoor is only 0.989..0.887 of that peak (7 of 7 flow cells non-monotone), so marginal_cop(T_out, 'buffer', 60 degC) is 2.034 at 10 degC but 1.880 at 20 degC (-7.6 %), which is the COP the simulation, _terminal_cost and _deferred_energy_cost price the tank at.
findings.mechanism: thermal_model.py:1328-1338 multiplies the linear base curve by Carnot(F,T_out)/Carnot(35 degC,T_out). The base curve's implied Carnot fraction falls from 0.33 at -20 degC to 0.17 at +25 degC (carnot_fraction_min/max), while the ratio's derivative in T_out has the sign of (T_ref - T_F) < 0, so the product turns over in mild weather - the opposite of a real unit at fixed flow temperature.

evidence.unit: count: cop_flow_cells_nonmonotone of 7; cop_ratio_20_over_peak_min = 0.8874 (flow 70), cop_ratio_20_over_peak_flow55 = 0.9427; marginal_cop_buffer60_out10 = 2.0339, _out20 = 1.8802
evidence.machine: Apple M1 8 GB (Darwin 25.6), python 3.13.1, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.18.1, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: ten other auditors on the box, load1 22-72 during the runs; every value is a count/ratio/residual/parity, contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: exact (0.5 K grid, diffs rounded at 1e-12)

findings.metric_definition: sign changes of dCOP/dT_out on a 0.5 K grid over [-25, 30] degC per flow temperature, and COP(20 degC)/COP(peak)

null_control.value: flow_temp=None: 0 sign changes; compute_cop_dhw: 0 violations in tank or outdoor temperature
null_control.note: only the Carnot flow branch turns over

reproduction_steps: read the CELL flow=F lines (argmax_out, ratio20/peak) and RESULT marginal_cop_buffer60_out10/out20
findings.proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py compute_cop: derive the flow derate from a Carnot fraction consistent with the base curve (eta = COP_ref*(T_ref-T_out)/T_ref at the reference flow, COP(F) = eta*T_F/(T_F-T_out) with the existing lift floor), then re-record the valve/wood fixtures.

findings.title: The planning grid steps wall-clock time: DST days plan 96 steps over 23 or 25 real hours
findings.claim: On every DST transition day tested (six, 2025-2027), 84 of the coordinator's 96 planning steps carry a price that is not the price in force at t0 + i*15 min real time (plain day: 0); the spring grid maps 96 labels onto 92 real instants and the production optimizer anchored as the coordinator anchors it books 6.0 kWh of the day's 29.96 kWh in the four non-existent 02:xx steps, while the autumn grid holds the step labelled 02:45 CEST for 75 real minutes at 6.0 kW.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py:5728/5849/6035 and optimizer.py:981/2033 build step instants as aware_local_midnight + timedelta(15*i min), which Python defines as wall-clock arithmetic; Tibber entries carry real offsets and are bisected by instant (_known_prices_for), so after the transition every step is one real hour off. price_model._entries_by_day already drops DST days for learning and tariff._window_slot carries fold; the plan grid does neither.

evidence.unit: count: dst_transition_steps_misaligned (min = max = 84 over 6 days); dst_spring_distinct_instants = 92, dst_spring_span_hours = 23, dst_autumn_span_hours = 25, dst_autumn_max_gap_min = 75, dst_spring_plan_phantom_kwh = 6.000 of 29.960

findings.title: sysid confidence cannot reach its 0.3 adoption gate at the default interval; a drifting sensor passes it biased
findings.claim: With the coordinator's default 30-minute sampling (_run_system_identification once per optimization cycle), SystemIdentification.identify's confidence for a noise-free experiment is 0.107 and its ceiling is 0.28 (< the 0.3 gate in _adopt_system_identification), so no result is ever adopted; at 15-minute sampling clean data scores 0.250 (rejected, UA exact) while a 0.10 / 0.15 K/h linear drift scores 0.304 / 0.341, is adopted, and carries UA -12 % / -24 % (tau +15 % / +32 %).
findings.mechanism: sysid.py:453-459: confidence = r2 * min(1, rows/20) * clip(excursion/2, 0.3, 1). A 2 h step + 2 h relax at 30-min samples gives 7 rows (0.35) and the 0.8 K comfort abort bounds the excursion factor at 0.8, ceiling 0.28; drift inflates the delta-T range (raising the excursion factor) while biasing the UA column.

evidence.unit: ratio: sysid_clean_confidence_30min (ceiling 0.280, gate 0.300); sysid_clean_confidence_15min = 0.250; sysid_drift_0.10Kph_mean_confidence = 0.304 with median_rel_err_UA = -0.1216; drift_0.15Kph: 0.341 / -0.2368

findings.title: wood_share is discontinuous at the flow curve when the HP tank sits within the switch margin
findings.claim: wood_share (docstring: 'continuous in w * Q_draw across every boundary') jumps from (wood-hp)/margin to 1.0 as wood_temp crosses flow_set while hp_temp is in (flow_set - margin, flow_set]: a jump of 1.0 in share at hp_temp = flow_set (13.44 kW of a 13.44 kW emitter draw moving between tanks for a 1e-6 K change) and 0.5 at flow_set - 1 K; _wood_share_vec reproduces it bitwise.
findings.mechanism: thermal_model.py:1108-1115: region 1 (wood >= flow_set) returns 1.0 while region 3 (both tanks at/below the curve) returns (wood - hp)/margin, which only reaches 1.0 when wood - hp >= margin; the two laws agree at the curve only for hp <= flow_set - margin.

evidence.machine: Apple M1 8 GB (Darwin 25.6), python 3.13.1, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.18.1, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: ten other auditors on the box, load1 22-72 during the runs; every value is a count/ratio/residual/parity, contention-immune

reproduction_steps: read CELL wood_share worst jump and RESULT wood_share_max_jump
